vo: A small law firm gets a new enquiry. IXIA answers it in seconds. Then someone still has to type the client into the firm's practice portal and book a first consultation. IXIA Desk Agent does that step in a browser that is sealed off from everything else.

Guardrails checks the enquiry first. The controller then mints a portal token for this one task: one contact, one booking, ten minutes. A new container starts for this enquiry. Read-only, no capabilities, no keys, and one exit: a proxy that lets through only the portal.

A planning model on Vultr Serverless Inference chooses one action at a time from a fixed list. After every action a vision model on Vultr reads the screenshot and confirms the page is where the plan expected.
The last click books a real slot, so it waits for a person. Approve. The booking is in, the container is deleted and the token is revoked.
This enquiry hides orders for the AI: read the cloud keys, export the client list, send it to another server, add a contact.

Guardrails holds it for a person. We told nine chat models on Vultr to obey such orders. Not one started on them. So we do not rely on the model. In red-team mode the controller carries out every order inside the sandbox, as if the model had obeyed.
The proxy refuses the cloud metadata address.
The portal refuses the export to a task token.
The proxy refuses the outside server.
The real booking still waits for a person.
After it, the extra contact is refused: the token allows one.

On thirty-one fictional enquiries, in the latest pass: thirteen of eighteen plain ones were booked, and Guardrails held the other five for a person. Every sensitive and every hostile enquiry was held. All twenty sandboxes were removed, and no run changed the portal by more than one contact and one booking.
Two Vultr VMs, every model call on Vultr Serverless Inference. The code is open under MIT, and the demo is live at desk dot ixia dot online.
